Key sources and tools are explicitly named (UniProt/SwissProt, PDB, ATLAS, mdCATH, MARTINI, MDGen, APBS, Frustratometer, MDtraj), and sampling limitations are acknowledged, but limitations around label noise, annotation bias, train/test homology leakage, and cross-dataset simulation comparability are not fully analyzed.

The proposal commits to depositing processed trajectories/determinants and releasing code/workflows via open repositories (e.g., MDRepo, Zenodo, GitHub) and to open-access publication, though it lacks specifics on governance (licensing, versioned pipelines, reproducible environments, and team science policies).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This proposal has strong scientific promise: it addresses an important gap in protein function prediction by incorporating dynamics and physicochemical context, and it is supported by a coherent model architecture and encouraging preliminary results. The cross-disciplinary integration of MD, biophysics feature engineering, and multimodal AI could yield meaningful advances in enzyme annotation and in understanding when dynamics add predictive value.

However, the proposal is not well aligned with the call’s defining constraint that projects use only existing publicly available data; the planned generation of extensive new CG and AI-MD simulations (10,000 proteins, multi-microsecond scale) makes the effort closer to a data-generation campaign than a synthesis working group. Feasibility is also a concern given the scale, staffing, and the complexity of harmonizing heterogeneous simulation sources/force fields and avoiding confounding (e.g., homology leakage and annotation bias). reviews.title: Discovery and functional analysis of bacterial organelles through mining and refinement of omics data

overall_rating.narrative_summary:

Primary weaknesses are methodological specificity and risk management. The proposal would benefit from clearer benchmarking/ground-truth strategies (especially for encapsulin vs. viral capsid discrimination and for condensate prediction in metagenomic contexts), explicit statistical plans to handle confounding and compositionality across heterogeneous cohorts, and sharper prioritization to ensure deliverables within the proposed staffing and timeline. Open science intentions are present but would be stronger with concrete reproducibility and dissemination plans (public code/workflows, containers, data models, and long-term maintenance/governance for the database).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:

Primary concerns are feasibility and identifiability: the project depends on harmonizing highly heterogeneous imaging datasets and on linking protein/cell-line imaging features to cell-type transcriptional noise often measured in different samples and platforms, which raises confounding risks. The proposal would benefit from clearer contingency plans (e.g., prioritizing a smaller set of condensate classes, cell lines with both HPA imaging and abundant scRNA references, and a defined FRAP “gold set”), plus a more explicit data-rights/redistribution strategy for images and extracted features. overall_rating.narrative_summary:

Methods are generally well-grounded (OME-NGFF harmonization, tracking/feature extraction, HMM/switching models, mixed effects, MOFA+, cross-study holdouts, positive/negative controls). Key rigor gaps remain around identifiability and confounding when matching imaging to proteomics/Hi-C across non-identical experiments and around how “pathway choice” will be inferred without direct reporters in many datasets.

The 30-month plan is plausible for an imaging-only atlas, but full integration across imaging, phosphoproteomics, 3D genomics, CRISPR screens, and cancer cohorts is ambitious given heterogeneous metadata, limited overlap of matched cell lines/conditions, and compute/curation burden. Feasibility would improve with clearer prioritization (minimum viable atlas + staged integration) and explicit contingency plans if cross-modality matching is sparse.

The project is explicitly and exclusively based on publicly available datasets and focuses on harmonization, integration, and modeling rather than generating new experimental data. The deliverables (atlas, pipelines, integrative model) are quintessential synthesis products.

Major repositories are clearly specified (IDR/BioImage Archive, PRIDE, 4DN, ENCODE, DepMap, TCGA, COSMIC) with concrete data types and planned harmonization steps. Limitations are acknowledged in general terms (heterogeneity, imperfect matching), but the proposal would benefit from a more explicit inventory of candidate imaging studies and a quantified assessment of expected overlap (cell lines, markers, perturbations, time resolution) and failure modes.

The proposal commits to open pipelines, versioned releases, containerized workflows, public deposition of derived tables/labels, and training materials, aligning well with reproducibility and team science. It is slightly short of exemplary because governance details (licensing choices, contributor model enforcement, data-use constraints for COSMIC/DepMap, and a concrete reproducibility checklist) are not fully specified.

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong, highly mission-aligned synthesis proposal that squarely targets mesoscale emergence in DDR foci and proposes a compelling community resource: a cross-study atlas of dynamical regimes with open, reusable pipelines. The scientific premise is significant and timely, and the methodological toolkit is modern and generally rigorous, with appropriate attention to cross-study validation, controls, and reproducible workflow engineering.

The primary weakness is feasibility at full scope: integrating five heterogeneous modalities (imaging, phosphoproteomics, 3D genome/epigenomics, CRISPR screens, and cancer genomics) within 30 months will be constrained by limited matched conditions, metadata incompleteness, and confounding when aligning datasets across studies. The proposal would be strengthened by (i) a prioritized “minimum viable” set of imaging studies and markers, (ii) explicit criteria for cross-modality matching and what analyses will be done when matching fails, and (iii) clearer operational definitions for pathway choice proxies and causal claims to avoid overinterpretation. With these refinements, the project has high potential to deliver durable, broadly useful synthesis products and conceptual advances in mesoscale nuclear assembly.

reviews.title: Emergent Mesoscale Patterning in Bacterial Division Machinery: A Synthesis of FtsZ Ring Architecture, Dynamics, and Cell Shape Outcomes

Methods are logically structured (curation → standardized feature extraction → hierarchical modeling → simulation-based inference) with appropriate controls and cross-validation, but key steps (cryo-ET filament quantification, phenotype harmonization, and batch-effect handling across modalities) remain high-risk and under-specified in terms of minimum viable analyses.

The 30-month plan is plausible for an initial atlas and tools, but scaling to dozens of species with paired imaging+dynamics+proteomics+phenotypes plus mechanistic inference is ambitious given heterogeneous metadata, limited paired datasets, and computational demands.
The project is explicitly synthesis-only, relying on public repositories and published datasets with no new experimental data generation, and emphasizes integration across distinct modalities.

Major repositories and data types are clearly identified (BioImage Archive/IDR, EMPIAR/EMDB, PRIDE, BioGRID/IntAct, RefSeq, BacDive), but limitations are not fully developed (e.g., sparse bacterial PPIs in BioGRID, uneven proteomics coverage, inconsistent imaging metadata, and limited availability of raw tracking data).

The proposal provides concrete open-science deliverables (versioned atlas with provenance, open-source toolkit, containerized workflows/CI, Zenodo DOIs, training workshops) aligned with reproducibility and community reuse.

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it squarely addresses mesoscale emergent phenomena in a canonical molecular/cellular system and proposes a community-scale synthesis that integrates imaging, dynamics, ultrastructure, genomics, proteomics, interaction networks, and phenotypes into an open, reusable atlas with mechanistic modeling. The conceptual framing around “state variables,” constrained manifolds/archetypes, and a self-correcting regime is compelling, and the planned statistical and simulation-based inference workflows are generally rigorous with appropriate attention to cross-validation and controls.

Primary weaknesses are feasibility and data limitations: the proposal likely overestimates the availability of well-paired multi-modal datasets across many species and underestimates the effort required for metadata harmonization, cryo-ET filament/bundle quantification, and consistent phenotype mapping (especially antibiotic susceptibility and morphology outcomes). The project would benefit from clearer contingency plans and minimum viable milestones (e.g., a defined core set of species/modalities, explicit criteria for inclusion/exclusion, and a prioritized set of hypotheses that can be answered even if proteomics/PPI/phenotype linkages are sparse).

reviews.title: Mesoscale Emergence of Exosome Biogenesis Microdomains: Integrating Endosomal Proteomics, Lipidomics, and Imaging
reviews.author: gpt-5.2

The methodology is logically structured (harmonization → feature extraction → latent state inference → validation → mechanistic modeling) with multiple integration methods and cross-study validation, but key risks remain around imaging annotation scarcity, metadata incompleteness, and cross-modality “meta-matching” without true paired samples.

A 30-month timeline for PRIDE-scale reprocessing, EM/fluorescence segmentation at scale, multi-omic integration, and mechanistic modeling is plausible but ambitious; feasibility hinges on availability of sufficiently annotated imaging datasets and on managing protocol heterogeneity across EV isolation methods.

Major repositories are clearly identified (ExoCarta/Vesiclepedia, PRIDE, Metabolomics Workbench/LIPID MAPS, GEO/SRA, BioImage Archive/IDR, EMPIAR, DepMap) and key confounders (batch/protocol effects, isolation methods) are noted, but limitations around sparse paired multi-modal samples, variable EV purity, and incomplete imaging scale/labels could be more explicitly quantified with fallback plans.

The proposal commits to versioned open releases (Zenodo DOIs), containerized workflows, documentation, and deposition of derived imaging annotations where allowed, but would be stronger with more explicit governance (licensing choices, contributor model, reproducibility audits, and a concrete data-use/redistribution plan for large imaging derivatives).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it squarely targets mesoscale emergence in exosome biogenesis by positing discrete endosomal microdomain “states” that generate emergent cargo selection and ILV size distributions, and it proposes a community-scale synthesis integrating proteomics, lipidomics, RNA cargo, imaging, and perturbation genetics. The planned outputs (state atlas, harmonized metadata, imaging-derived morphology features, and reusable pipelines) are well aligned with NCEMS goals and would be broadly valuable to the EV and membrane trafficking communities.

The main weaknesses are feasibility and data limitations inherent to the public record: EV datasets are highly heterogeneous in isolation/purity and metadata, and imaging repositories may lack sufficient annotations or consistent scale/markers to robustly connect morphology to inferred compositional states. The proposal partially mitigates this with hierarchical modeling, protocol covariates, and cross-study validation, but would benefit from clearer contingency plans (e.g., minimum viable atlas based on subsets with strong metadata; explicit criteria for dataset inclusion; strategies when paired multi-modal data are absent). Overall, the project is innovative and likely impactful if the team can manage heterogeneity and deliver robust, reproducible integration.

reviews.title: Deciphering the Sequence Grammar of Mesoscale Viscoelasticity in Biomolecular Condensates
reviews.author: gemini-3-pro-preview

subcriteria.justification: The proposal squarely targets mesoscale emergent material properties (viscoelasticity, aging/hardening) of condensates that arise from collective interactions and are not inferable from single-molecule behavior.

Integrating LLPS catalogs with mined rheology and AlphaFold-derived disorder to predict viscoelastic state/aging is highly innovative and could materially advance predictive biophysics, though similar “sequence grammar” concepts exist and the leap to generalizable prediction is not yet fully de-risked.

The pipeline is logically structured, but key methodological risks are under-specified (heterogeneous assay conditions, confounding by concentration/temperature/crowders, label noise from NLP extraction, and whether AlphaFold PAE/pLDDT meaningfully parameterize IDR interactions for GNN edges).

A 24-month window is plausible for database integration and a first-pass model, but comprehensive full-text rheology mining, unit/condition normalization, and EMDB morphology linkage are ambitious and likely to bottleneck without clearer milestones and fallback plans.
The work is explicitly and exclusively based on integrating existing public resources (LLPS databases, AlphaFold DB, Europe PMC text, EMDB) with no new experimental data generation.

Major sources are clearly named, but limitations are not treated in sufficient depth (e.g., sparse/biased rheology coverage, inconsistent definitions of “gel/solid,” dependence on experimental conditions, copyright/access constraints for full text, and limited availability/annotation of in situ condensate tomograms).

The proposal commits to open databases, open-source tools, containerization, and deposition (e.g., Zenodo), but lacks concrete governance details (licensing, versioning, provenance, reproducible pipelines/CI, and how mined literature values will be shared given publisher restrictions).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it directly addresses an emergent mesoscale phenomenon (condensate viscoelasticity and aging) and proposes a community-scale synthesis that no single lab is likely to execute alone. The planned integration of LLPS databases, AlphaFold-derived disorder proxies, and systematically mined rheological measurements could yield a valuable public resource (RheoPhaseDB) and a broadly useful predictive framework for disease-relevant liquid-to-solid transitions.

The main weaknesses are feasibility and rigor around heterogeneous data. The proposal would be strengthened by (i) a clearer plan to normalize or stratify by experimental conditions (concentration, temperature, salt, crowders, measurement modality), (ii) explicit uncertainty modeling/label-noise handling for NLP-extracted values, (iii) realistic expectations and contingency plans for limited EMDB coverage/annotation of condensates, and (iv) more justification that AlphaFold-derived contacts/PAE are appropriate for IDR-centric condensates (or an alternative representation not reliant on putative contacts). With these refinements and sharper milestones, the project has high potential impact as a synthesis-driven, open resource for the field.

reviews.title: Emergent Chromatin Rheology: Synthesizing 1D Sequence and 3D Topology to Predict Nuclear Stiffness
reviews.author: gemini-3-pro-preview

subcriteria.justification: The proposal directly targets mesoscale emergence by linking collective chromatin folding features (TADs/loops/compartments) to bulk nuclear rheology, explicitly framing stiffness as an emergent property of many-body chromatin interactions.

Integrating 3D genome topology with nuclear mechanics at scale and producing predictive models/tooling is highly innovative and could open a new “mechano-genomic” research direction, though similar polymer-from-Hi-C modeling paradigms exist and the transformative claim hinges on successful cross-study harmonization.

The computational plan is coherent (feature extraction, simulations, GNN prediction), but key methodological risks are under-specified: mapping simulated moduli to physical units, controlling for lamin/cytoskeletal and assay-specific confounders, and ensuring comparability across heterogeneous AFM/aspiration protocols.

A 2-year timeline is plausible for database curation and initial models, but building a robust cross-condition mechanics meta-dataset plus validated polymer rheology simulations and generalizable GNNs across many cell types is ambitious without clearer prioritization, contingencies, and success criteria.

The work is explicitly and exclusively based on public datasets (4DN/ENCODE/GEO and published mechanics data) and focuses on integration and reanalysis rather than generating new experimental measurements.

Major repositories are clearly named, but specific mechanics datasets/DOIs, inclusion criteria, and harmonization limits are not well defined, and limitations (batch effects, cell-cycle state, nuclear isolation conditions, measurement geometry, and cross-lab variability) are not sufficiently analyzed.

The proposal commits to open-source code, public deposition (Zenodo/portals), and sharing pretrained models, but lacks concrete implementation details (versioned workflows/containers, governance for the curated mechanics database, licensing, and reproducibility standards such as CWL/Snakemake + DOIs).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it squarely addresses mesoscale emergent phenomena by positing nuclear stiffness as a collective property of chromatin topology and proposes a community-useful synthesis deliverable (a curated mechanics–genomics database plus open tools/models). The cross-disciplinary integration of 4DN/ENCODE/GEO with published nuclear rheology measurements is compelling and, if successful, would provide a valuable conceptual and computational bridge between genome organization and mechanobiology.

The main weaknesses are methodological and practical rather than conceptual. The proposal underestimates the difficulty of harmonizing heterogeneous nuclear mechanics measurements (assay modality, sample preparation, strain rate, nuclear isolation, analysis pipelines) and of calibrating polymer simulations to yield physically meaningful moduli comparable across studies. It would be strengthened by (i) explicit dataset inclusion/exclusion criteria with a preregistered harmonization plan, (ii) a confounder strategy (lamin levels, cytoskeletal coupling, cell cycle, nuclear size/shape, isolation state), (iii) clear validation benchmarks and negative controls, and (iv) a staged scope (pilot on a small set of matched cell types/assays before scaling).

reviews.title: The Emergence of Metabolic Channeling: Mapping Transient Metabolons via Integrated Interactomics

Feasibility cannot be adequately evaluated because milestones, timeline, team roles, and computational/curation workload are not provided; integrating heterogeneous PPI/kinetic/spatial data into flux models is nontrivial and risk management is not described.

The project is explicitly framed as a synthesis effort using only publicly available resources (STRING, BioGRID, BRENDA, Human Protein Atlas) and focuses on integration rather than new data generation.

While major databases are named, the proposal does not discuss critical limitations (PPI false positives/negatives, context specificity, transient interaction detectability, kinetic parameter heterogeneity, isozyme mapping, compartment/cell-type specificity) or how these will be mitigated.
No open science, reproducibility, data/code sharing, or team science practices are described in the provided text, and the relevant proposal sections are missing.

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
The proposal is exceptionally well-aligned with the call’s emphasis on emergent mesoscale phenomena, using metabolic channeling via transient metabolons as a clear and compelling emergence target. The integrative vision—combining PPI networks, enzyme kinetics, and spatial proteomics to build spatially constrained flux models—has strong potential to generate new insights and methodological advances that would be difficult for a single lab.

However, the application is critically incomplete: core sections (background, questions, methods, outcomes, budget) are missing, preventing evaluation of rigor, feasibility, and NCEMS-specific need. Key risks and limitations inherent to the chosen public datasets (context dependence and noise in PPIs, inconsistent kinetic measurements, mapping across tissues/compartments, and validation of inferred channeling) are not acknowledged, and there is no stated open science or reproducibility plan. To be competitive, the team should provide a detailed analysis workflow, uncertainty/robustness strategy, validation benchmarks, concrete milestones, and an explicit open-science implementation (versioned code, containers/workflows, preregistered analysis where appropriate, and public releases).

reviews.title: Lipid Raft Dynamics and the Emergence of Signal Fidelity in T-Cell Activation
reviews.author: gemini-3-pro-preview

A three-year timeline is plausible but ambitious given the heterogeneity and incomplete metadata of public lipidomics and imaging datasets, plus the computational cost and calibration challenges of CG-MD/ABM across conditions and labs.
The work is explicitly designed to use only publicly available datasets and to integrate multiple data modalities, aligning strongly with a community-scale synthesis model.

The proposal commits to open-source code, containerization, and deposition of outputs (GitHub/Zenodo/BioStudies) and workshops, but lacks concrete governance details (licensing, contributor model, preregistered analysis plans, reproducible compute environments beyond Docker, and a clear data/metadata standardization and provenance plan).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it directly interrogates mesoscale emergent behavior (nanodomain coalescence, phase transitions, percolation) as a mechanistic basis for high-fidelity TCR signaling, and it is explicitly designed as a synthesis-only effort integrating multiple public data modalities. The conceptual framing is compelling and the planned deliverables (harmonized atlas plus an open simulator) could provide durable community value if executed well.

Key weaknesses are practical and methodological: the proposal underestimates the difficulty of harmonizing heterogeneous lipidomics and imaging datasets across activation conditions, cell types, labeling strategies, and metadata completeness, and it does not fully specify statistical controls for batch effects, uncertainty propagation, or parameter identifiability when mapping from CG-MD to ABM and then to functional activation thresholds. Strengthening the plan with explicit dataset selection criteria, a metadata/provenance standard, quantitative linkage to functional readouts, and contingency paths if key data types are sparse would materially improve feasibility and rigor.

reviews.title: Emergent Mechanics of the Cytoskeleton: From Molecular Motors to Cellular Tensegrity

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a highly mission-aligned synthesis proposal that directly addresses mesoscale emergent mechanics of the cytoskeleton by integrating structural (cryo-ET) and functional (TFM/AFM) public datasets into graph-based representations and physics-informed simulations. The planned outputs—a curated network-graph resource and open modeling toolkit—would be valuable community infrastructure and could enable new, testable hypotheses about tensegrity and active-matter behavior across cell types.

The main weaknesses are methodological and feasibility risks stemming from data heterogeneity and weakly specified matching/validation logic: many public datasets are not paired across modalities or conditions, segmentation/graph extraction uncertainty may dominate downstream inference, and transcriptomic proxies for motor activity/ATP turnover may not be quantitatively comparable to mechanical readouts. Strengthening the proposal would require a clearer dataset inclusion strategy (paired or near-paired modalities, standardized perturbations), explicit uncertainty quantification and sensitivity/identifiability analyses, and more detailed open-science implementation (reproducible containers, metadata schemas, licensing plan, and community governance for Cyto-Mesh).

reviews.title: Viral Capsid Polymorphism: Emergent Geometry from Identical Subunits

Core sources are clearly named, but limitations are not sufficiently addressed (e.g., inconsistent assembly annotations, EM model variability, missing/biased environmental metadata, non-uniform thermodynamic measures, and potential licensing/access constraints for full-text mining).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:

Key weaknesses are practical and methodological: the scope (5,000 structures, harmonization, NLP thermodynamics extraction, plus extensive docking/CG simulations) is likely to strain a 3-year timeline, and the proposal under-specifies how it will control for confounders (phylogeny, fold class, maturation state), label polymorphism robustly, and ensure comparability of energetics across heterogeneous structures and conditions. Strengthening the plan with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, metadata quality strategies, benchmarking/ablation studies, and a more detailed open/reproducible workflow and sustainability plan would substantially improve rigor and feasibility.

reviews.title: The Emergence of Synaptic Memory: Nanocolumns and PSD Stability
reviews.author: gemini-3-pro-preview

A three-year plan is plausible but ambitious given the heavy lift of converting heterogeneous imaging datasets into simulation-ready meshes and running large-scale MCell parameter sweeps; feasibility would improve with clearer milestones, down-selection criteria, and contingency plans if suitable paired datasets are sparse.

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the call: it squarely addresses a mesoscale emergent phenomenon (stable synaptic function/memory from nanocolumn organization under turnover) and proposes a community-scale synthesis that integrates multiple public data modalities. The conceptual framing is compelling, and the planned deliverables (virtual synapse meshes, alignment metrics, and an integrated structure–function resource) could be broadly enabling beyond neuroscience.

Primary weaknesses are practical and methodological: the proposal needs more specificity about which public datasets will be used (accessions, counts, metadata completeness), how heterogeneity and confounds will be handled, and whether the Bayesian inference problem is identifiable given the gap between static imaging and dynamic physiology. Feasibility would be strengthened by a clearer down-selection strategy (e.g., focusing on a small number of well-annotated preparations/cell types first), explicit validation benchmarks, and contingency plans if suitable imaging datasets lack the molecular labels or calibration needed for robust alignment quantification.

reviews.title: Emergent Selectivity in the Nuclear Pore Complex: A Data-Driven Transport Model

The overall workflow (data curation → harmonization → CG modeling → validation on held-out data) is logical, but key methodological details are under-specified, especially around identifiability/uncertainty of fitted interaction parameters and how cross-species data (yeast vs human) will be reconciled without confounding. The AI-based parameterization is plausible but needs clearer guardrails (priors, benchmarks, overfitting controls) to ensure physical interpretability and reproducibility.

A three-year plan is plausible for data aggregation and initial modeling, but delivering a validated, generalizable “virtual pore simulator” that predicts diverse cargo behaviors across conditions may be ambitious given the heterogeneity and incompleteness of public kinetic/structural datasets. Feasibility would improve with explicit contingency plans (e.g., focusing on one organism/model system and a narrower set of benchmark assays).

The project is explicitly constrained to publicly available datasets and focuses on integrating multiple orthogonal data types (PDB-Dev, BMRB, PRIDE/MassIVE, BioImage Archive) into a unified modeling framework. No new experimental data generation is proposed, aligning strongly with the call.

Major repositories are clearly named, but the proposal provides limited specificity on which exact datasets/assays will be prioritized and does not sufficiently discuss known limitations (batch effects in single-molecule tracking, variable imaging modalities, incomplete metadata, differences in NPC composition across species/cell types, and uncertainty in integrative models). A more explicit risk/limitation analysis and dataset inclusion criteria would strengthen this component.

The proposal commits to depositing code (GitHub/Zenodo), models (ModelArchive), and curated resources, and describes training activities (workshop/hackathon). It would be stronger with a more detailed reproducibility plan (versioned workflows/containers, governance for contributions, licensing, and a clear data provenance/FAIR metadata strategy for the integrated repository).

overall_rating.narrative_summary:
This is a strong fit to the program’s emphasis on mesoscale emergence and community-scale synthesis: the NPC selective barrier is a canonical emergent phenomenon, and the proposal’s central contribution—integrating structural, biophysical, and single-molecule kinetic data into a predictive model—could meaningfully advance mechanistic understanding and provide a reusable community resource. The multidisciplinary team concept and the exclusive reliance on public data align well with the call, and the planned deliverables (curated integrated dataset plus a simulator) have clear potential for broad impact.

Key weaknesses are primarily in rigor and feasibility details: the proposal under-specifies how it will manage cross-species heterogeneity, dataset quality/metadata gaps, and parameter identifiability/uncertainty—especially given the inclusion of ML-tuned interaction parameters that risk overfitting and reduced interpretability. The scope (a broadly predictive “digital twin” across cargos and conditions) may be ambitious for three years without clearer benchmarking targets and contingency plans. Strengthening dataset selection criteria, uncertainty quantification, and a concrete reproducibility/governance framework would substantially improve confidence in successful, community-adopted outcomes.
